Several source families and regions still lack a closed discovery boundary.

objective_rules.rule: One denominator unit is one externally named, finite, ongoing summit or high-point challenge, award, or completion register with a stable roster or version key.

Qualification needs either a federation, club, government, or author-maintained award/register, or a named challenge with an authoritative public roster and at least ten years of documented completion practice.
Members must be summits or jurisdiction high points. The roster must be finite and identify each member well enough to build a reproducible crosswalk.

Count one current challenge once. Retired editions, map-datum editions, winter rounds, and alternative accepted rosters are variants of that unit unless a keeper gives each a distinct award or register.
A parent and subset may both count only when the keeper offers distinct awards or registers. A regional browse slice of a global database is not a second unit.

Exclude app-made collections, raw database filters, arbitrary threshold cuts with no outside challenge tradition, and a product-selected subset of another page. A real outside named source can cure the last defect, as Idaho's 12ers does.
Qualification does not depend on whether Peaks can import the roster. Keep a qualifying rights-blocked list in the denominator and mark it blocked.
Do not impose an after-the-fact minimum or maximum member count. Three-peak, five-peak, nine-peak, and multi-thousand-peak registers qualify when they meet the same proof rule.
A classic route or timed round qualifies only when it also has a stable named summit roster and an ongoing cumulative completion tradition.
Count Peaks coverage only when the product list ID has the current accepted roster key and exact membership. A retired roster or wrong count is zero coverage until corrected.
Use no geographic quota, but report discovery coverage by region and leave the registry open where primary-source discovery is incomplete.

regional_bias.finding: The proposed set was selected around the product's US imports, not through a closed world discovery method. The 83-unit lower bound still leans toward North America and Britain/Ireland. Asia, Africa, South America, continental Europe outside Britain/Ireland, and Australasia need deeper family-level discovery.

conclusion.plain_statement: Peaks covers 22 of this confirmed 83-unit lower bound now. The ready exact pull-request stack would raise that to 38, four short of the 42 needed for a majority of 83. A separate six-unit cross-region tranche could reach 44 only after its rights, imports, and reviews are complete. None of these figures proves a worldwide share.
conclusion.rights_statement: Qualifying blocked lists remain in the 83. Rights blocks, rights uncertainty, and source defects stay visible; none can be erased to make import or coverage figures look better.
